Splitting this using a standard work-breakdown structure: numbered pieces, each with a dictionary entry so scope doesn't overlap and ownership is unambiguous. I'll also write down the multi-currency deferral explicitly since that's the kind of undocumented decision that causes scope disputes later.

## Scope Boundary (write this down before assigning work)

**Out of scope this quarter: Multi-currency support.** Team Billing ships single-currency only (assume USD unless told otherwise). Multi-currency is deferred to a later release. This affects the billing engine (no currency conversion/rounding logic), invoice generator (no localized currency formatting), and usage-tracking service (no currency-tagged usage records). Anyone touching those three pieces should treat currency as a fixed, hardcoded constant, not a parameter — building loose hooks for future multi-currency is out of scope too and shouldn't be silently added.

## 1.0 Team Billing Subsystem

### 1.1 Billing Engine
**Definition:** Calculates what a team owes based on plan, usage, and pricing rules.
**Includes:** Rate/plan lookup, charge calculation logic, proration for mid-cycle changes, discount/credit application.
**Excludes:** Currency conversion (deferred), payment collection (1.2), invoice formatting/PDF (1.3), raw usage collection (1.4).
**Depends on:** Usage data from 1.4.
**Done when:** Given a team's plan + usage, produces a correct charge total, testable independent of UI or invoicing.

### 1.2 Payment-Method Vault
**Definition:** Securely stores and manages how a team pays (cards, ACH, etc.).
**Includes:** Storing/tokenizing payment methods, CRUD for methods, default-method selection, PCI-relevant handling.
**Excludes:** Charge calculation (1.1), actually triggering charges/invoice payment flow (1.3), displaying payment info (1.5 may read from this, not own it).
**Depends on:** Nothing internal — can start immediately, in parallel with everything else.
**Done when:** A team can add/remove/select a payment method via API, and other pieces can retrieve a valid method to charge.

### 1.3 Invoice Generator
**Definition:** Turns a calculated charge into a formal invoice and handles the billing document lifecycle.
**Includes:** Invoice creation from billing engine output, line-item formatting, invoice states (draft/sent/paid/void), triggering payment via the vault.
**Excludes:** Charge calculation itself (1.1), currency localization (deferred), payment method storage (1.2), viewing UI (1.5).
**Depends on:** Output from 1.1, methods from 1.2.
**Done when:** A charge from the billing engine becomes a retrievable invoice with correct line items and status.

### 1.4 Usage-Tracking Service
**Definition:** Captures and stores what a team actually used, as the raw input to billing.
**Includes:** Event/metric ingestion, aggregation per billing period, exposing usage data to the billing engine.
**Excludes:** Any charge calculation (1.1), currency tagging (deferred), displaying usage to users (1.5 may consume, not own).
**Depends on:** Nothing internal — can start immediately.
**Done when:** Billing engine can query accurate, period-bounded usage totals for any team.

### 1.5 Admin Dashboard
**Definition:** UI for viewing a team's bills, invoices, and usage.
**Includes:** Views for invoice history, current usage, payment method on file (read-only or manage via 1.2's API).
**Excludes:** Any calculation logic, invoice generation logic, payment storage logic — this piece only *displays* data owned by 1.1–1.4.
**Depends on:** Read APIs from 1.1/1.3/1.4/1.2.
**Done when:** An admin can view a team's current bill, past invoices, and usage without needing another tool.

## Sequencing note for assignment
1.2 (Vault) and 1.4 (Usage Tracking) have no internal dependencies — assign these first so they can run in parallel. 1.1 (Billing Engine) needs 1.4 to be far enough along to have a usage data shape to build against. 1.3 (Invoice Generator) needs 1.1 and 1.2 in a usable state. 1.5 (Dashboard) is downstream of all four and will lag behind unless someone builds against mocked APIs early.

This covers 100% of this quarter's Team Billing work with no overlap between pieces — every piece of functionality has exactly one owner. Want me to turn this into tickets/issues, or adjust any of the boundaries (e.g., should the dashboard also let admins manage payment methods, or strictly view-only)?
